reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program (Michigan, focus year 2021)

    Question: "Can a landlord evict a tenant for committing substantial damage to the property?"

    We model "evict" as the landlord's ability to recover possession via Michigan summary
    proceedings (MCL 600.5714), using the provided statutes.
*/

% --------------------------
% Jurisdiction / metadata
% --------------------------

jurisdiction(michigan).
focus_year(2021).

% --------------------------
% Scenario facts (only what the question states)
% --------------------------

landlord(l1).
tenant(t1).
premises(p1).

% Relationship: landlord rents premises to tenant (basic context needed to even discuss eviction).
landlord_of(l1, t1, p1).
in_possession(t1, p1).

% Factual statement from the question:
% "tenant commit(s) substantial damage to the property"
substantial_damage(t1, p1).

/* Helper that succeeds exactly when the encoded scenario statement is satisfied. */
scenario_statement :-
    jurisdiction(michigan),
    focus_year(2021),
    landlord(l1),
    tenant(t1),
    premises(p1),
    landlord_of(l1, t1, p1),
    in_possession(t1, p1),
    substantial_damage(t1, p1).

% --------------------------
% Statute translations
% --------------------------

/*
  MI Comp L  554.134 (2021) - termination notice rules (selected core structure).

  We encode notice-length rules as notice_days_required/4:
    notice_days_required(LeaseKind, Reason, RentIntervalDays, NoticeDays).

  This statute is not itself a "damage eviction" provision, but it affects when a tenancy
  is terminated by notice to quit, which is referenced by MCL 600.5714(1)(c)(iii).
*/

%  554.134(2): nonpayment -> written 7-day notice to quit
notice_days_required(at_will_or_otherwise, nonpayment_of_rent, _RentIntervalDays, 7) :- !.

%  554.134(4): controlled substance holdover after lease terminated per lease clause -> 24-hour notice
notice_days_required(_LeaseKind, controlled_substance_holdover_after_lease_clause_termination, _RentIntervalDays, 1) :- !.

%  554.134(1): at-will/sufferance -> 1 month notice, but if rent interval < 3 months then interval length
% For simplicity: if RentIntervalDays < 90, required notice equals RentIntervalDays; else 30 days.
notice_days_required(at_will_or_sufferance, ordinary_termination, RentIntervalDays, NoticeDays) :-
    integer(RentIntervalDays),
    ( RentIntervalDays < 90 -> NoticeDays = RentIntervalDays
    ; NoticeDays = 30
    ),
    !.

%  554.134(3): year-to-year -> notice terminates at expiration of 1 year from service (modeled as 365 days)
notice_days_required(year_to_year, ordinary_termination, _RentIntervalDays, 365) :- !.

% If inputs don't fit statute categories, fail (no silent defaults).
notice_days_required(_LeaseKind, _Reason, _RentIntervalDays, _NoticeDays) :-
    fail.

% --------------------------
% MI Comp L  600.5714 (2021) - summary proceedings grounds
% --------------------------

/*
   600.5714(1): A person entitled to possession may recover possession by summary proceedings in listed circumstances.

  We encode each circumstance as legal_summary_proceedings_ground/4:
    legal_summary_proceedings_ground(Ground, Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

  NOTE: The question is about property damage. That corresponds most closely to  600.5714(1)(d),
  which requires (among other things) extensive *and continuing* physical injury, discovery within
  90 days, a demand for possession, and then 7 days of neglect/refusal to vacate or repair.
*/

% "Entitled to possession" - minimal modeled assumption: the landlord of the premises is a person entitled.
% (The statute begins with this prerequisite; we keep it explicit and scenario-based.)
entitled_to_possession(Landlord, Premises) :-
    landlord_of(Landlord, _Tenant, Premises).

/*  600.5714(1)(a): nonpayment + 7-day written demand + still holding over */
legal_summary_proceedings_ground(nonpayment_7_day_demand, Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    entitled_to_possession(Landlord, Premises),
    in_possession(Tenant, Premises),
    nonpayment_of_rent(Tenant, Premises),
    written_demand_served(Landlord, Tenant, Premises, nonpayment_of_rent, DemandDaysAgo),
    integer(DemandDaysAgo),
    DemandDaysAgo >= 7.

/*  600.5714(1)(b): controlled substances + police report + 24-hour demand + holding over */
legal_summary_proceedings_ground(controlled_substance_24_hour_demand, Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    entitled_to_possession(Landlord, Premises),
    in_possession(Tenant, Premises),
    controlled_substance_on_premises_by_tenant_or_control(Tenant, Premises),
    formal_police_report_filed(Tenant, Premises, controlled_substance),
    written_demand_served(Landlord, Tenant, Premises, controlled_substance_lease_clause_termination, DemandDaysAgo),
    integer(DemandDaysAgo),
    DemandDaysAgo >= 1.

/*  600.5714(1)(c): holding over after various terminations (modeled abstractly) */
legal_summary_proceedings_ground(holding_over_after_termination, Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    entitled_to_possession(Landlord, Premises),
    in_possession(Tenant, Premises),
    lease_terminated(Tenant, Premises, termination_power_in_lease_or_implied_by_law).

legal_summary_proceedings_ground(holding_over_after_term_expires, Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    entitled_to_possession(Landlord, Premises),
    in_possession(Tenant, Premises),
    lease_term_expired(Tenant, Premises).

legal_summary_proceedings_ground(holding_over_after_554_134_notice_to_quit, Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    entitled_to_possession(Landlord, Premises),
    in_possession(Tenant, Premises),
    notice_to_quit_served_under_554_134(Tenant, Premises, NoticeDaysRequired),
    integer(NoticeDaysRequired),
    notice_days_elapsed_since_service(Tenant, Premises, ElapsedDays),
    integer(ElapsedDays),
    ElapsedDays >= NoticeDaysRequired.

/*  600.5714(1)(d): serious & continuing health hazard OR extensive & continuing physical injury,
   discovered not earlier than 90 days before proceedings, plus 7-day demand and no vacate/repair.
*/
legal_summary_proceedings_ground(extensive_continuing_injury_or_health_hazard_7_day_demand, Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    entitled_to_possession(Landlord, Premises),
    in_possession(Tenant, Premises),
    willful_or_negligent(Tenant, Premises),
    (
        serious_and_continuing_health_hazard(Tenant, Premises)
    ;
        extensive_and_continuing_physical_injury(Tenant, Premises)
    ),
    discovered_within_last_90_days(Landlord, Premises),
    written_demand_served(Landlord, Tenant, Premises, damage_or_hazard, DemandDaysAgo),
    integer(DemandDaysAgo),
    DemandDaysAgo >= 7,
    ( neglects_or_refuses_to_deliver_possession(Tenant, Premises)
    ; neglects_or_refuses_to_substantially_restore_or_repair(Tenant, Premises)
    ).

/*  600.5714(1)(e): physical injury/threat + police notified + 7-day notice to quit; exceptions omitted here */
legal_summary_proceedings_ground(physical_injury_or_threat_7_day_notice, Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    entitled_to_possession(Landlord, Premises),
    in_possession(Tenant, Premises),
    physical_injury_or_threat_on_landlord_property(Tenant, Premises),
    police_notified(Tenant, Premises, physical_injury_or_threat),
    written_notice_to_quit_served(Landlord, Tenant, Premises, physical_injury_or_threat, NoticeDaysAgo),
    integer(NoticeDaysAgo),
    NoticeDaysAgo >= 7.

%  600.5714(1)(f)-(h) omitted from scenario reasoning; would be added as additional grounds similarly.

% A landlord can (statutorily) use summary proceedings to recover possession if any ground holds.
legal_can_recover_possession(Landlord, Tenant, Premises) :-
    legal_summary_proceedings_ground(_Ground, Landlord, Tenant, Premises).

% --------------------------
% Linking "substantial damage" to statutory concepts (without over-assuming)
% --------------------------

% We conservatively map "substantial damage" to "extensive physical injury" only.
% The statute requires "extensive AND continuing" and also willful/negligent plus notice/demand.
extensive_physical_injury(Tenant, Premises) :-
    substantial_damage(Tenant, Premises).

extensive_and_continuing_physical_injury(Tenant, Premises) :-
    extensive_physical_injury(Tenant, Premises),
    continuing_physical_injury(Tenant, Premises).

% --------------------------
% Missing-fact placeholders (intentionally false unless provided as facts)
% --------------------------
% These predicates are defined so the program is complete and warning-free.
% They fail unless a matching fact is asserted in the scenario.

nonpayment_of_rent(_Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
controlled_substance_on_premises_by_tenant_or_control(_Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
formal_police_report_filed(_Tenant, _Premises, _Type) :- fail.

lease_terminated(_Tenant, _Premises, _How) :- fail.
lease_term_expired(_Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.

notice_to_quit_served_under_554_134(_Tenant, _Premises, _NoticeDaysRequired) :- fail.
notice_days_elapsed_since_service(_Tenant, _Premises, _ElapsedDays) :- fail.

willful_or_negligent(_Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
serious_and_continuing_health_hazard(_Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
continuing_physical_injury(_Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
discovered_within_last_90_days(_Landlord, _Premises) :- fail.

written_demand_served(_Landlord, _Tenant, _Premises, _Reason, _DemandDaysAgo) :- fail.
neglects_or_refuses_to_deliver_possession(_Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
neglects_or_refuses_to_substantially_restore_or_repair(_Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.

physical_injury_or_threat_on_landlord_property(_Tenant, _Premises) :- fail.
police_notified(_Tenant, _Premises, _Type) :- fail.
written_notice_to_quit_served(_Landlord, _Tenant, _Premises, _Reason, _NoticeDaysAgo) :- fail.

% --------------------------
% Answer logic
% --------------------------

/*
  The question asks if a landlord can evict for substantial damage.
  Under the provided statutes, eviction via summary proceedings for property damage
  requires the additional elements in MCL 600.5714(1)(d) (notice/demand + continuing injury/hazard etc.).
  Because the scenario statement provides only "substantial damage" and no additional elements,
  we cannot derive that eviction is permitted from these statutes.
*/

eviction_allowed_in_scenario :-
    scenario_statement,
    legal_can_recover_possession(l1, t1, p1).

housing_answer(yes) :-
    eviction_allowed_in_scenario,
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    !.

% --------------------------
% Main / initialization
% --------------------------

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Can a landlord evict a tenant for commiting substantial damage to the property?
